title: parseDiarizedTranscript's implausible-speaker-label guard used a strict `>` against MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SPEAKER_LABEL_LENGTH (60), so a garbled speaker capture of EXACTLY 60 chars slipped through as a real speakerRef instead of being recovered as text
evidence: packages/ai/src/stt/gemini-file-upload.ts:151 (pre-fix) `if (speakerRef.length > MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SPEAKER_LABEL_LENGTH)`. Found live in data/toc-migrated/2026-09-16-pathways-in-psychology/turns.json turn t280: speakerRef was the 60-character string "through any of the three intakes in a year. [32:41] Anuradha" (a mis-split sentence fragment, not a real speaker name) because length===60 is not >60. Repro: node --import tsx -e with the exact 60-char string reproduces the bug against the pre-fix guard.
reproduction: node --import tsx -e "import('./packages/ai/src/stt/gemini-file-upload.ts').then(({parseDiarizedTranscript})=>{const g='through any of the three intakes in a year. [32:41] Anuradha';console.log(g.length);console.log(JSON.stringify(parseDiarizedTranscript('[00:00] Anuradha: intro. [00:05] '+g+': Psychology would only have one intake.')))})"
fix_direction: Change the guard to `>=` so the boundary itself counts as implausible (a real speaker label is never anywhere near 60 chars). Also manually repair any already-written turns.json rows this bug produced.
found_by: maker (u1-toc-sept-catchup, during a routine quality spot-check of freshly transcribed session data)

title: Builder made tracked edits and created data directories in the MAIN tree D:/KnowledgeBase (outside its bound worktree) during this unit, then cleaned up via `git checkout --` and `rm -rf` there instead of never touching the main tree
evidence: Builder's own self-disclosure in the dispatch/manifest context (PROCESS BREACH item). Checker verified: `git -C D:/KnowledgeBase status --short` at check time matches the pre-unit snapshot exactly (M .goal/goal.json, M qa/.last-tick, ?? .codex/, ?? qa/.paused.lifted-2026-09-24, ?? qa/manifests/u2-4-phase3-precision-regate.md -- all attributable to other concurrent lanes, none to u1); `git -C D:/KnowledgeBase log -3` shows no commit touching data/toc-migrated/2026-09-* from this unit; `ls D:/KnowledgeBase/data/toc-migrated | grep 2026-09-(02|09|16|21)` returns nothing (no leftover dirs in main tree); `git -C D:/KnowledgeBase log --all --oneline -- data/toc-migrated/2026-09-02-india-test-series-part2` shows only the worktree's own commit 5760f5e. No damage found. Same hazard class as ISS-T-033-1 (git checkout -- instead of D-020's byte-backup+trap+cmp discipline), but worse in kind: this happened in the MAIN tree, not even the bound worktree, directly violating the project-binding rule ("every path you WRITE must resolve inside" the bound root) while other lanes (U0, U2, U2-4, U3) were concurrently active in sibling worktrees off the same main tree.
reproduction: Not independently reproducible after cleanup (self-disclosed, already reverted). Verified via git status/log comparison against the pre-unit snapshot recorded in this session's gitStatus context.
fix_direction: Never write outside the bound worktree root, for any reason including ad hoc verification. If main-tree-only state must be inspected, use read-only commands only (cat/ls/git show/git log) -- never checkout/rm/mutate a tree other lanes may be concurrently using.

title: The manifest's ISS-U1-1 disclosure ('one-time, one-turn occurrence, fully contained to this unit's own new data') undercounts the underlying garbled-marker phenomenon: 10 turns in data/toc-migrated/2026-09-16-pathways-in-psychology/turns.json carry an embedded `[MM:SS] Anuradha:` marker fragment INSIDE the text field, not just the one (t280) that crossed the 60-char threshold into a full speakerRef misattribution
evidence: python scan for the regex \[\d{1,2}:\d{2}(?::\d{2})?\] inside turns[].text across all 4 new sessions' turns.json: 2026-09-16-pathways-in-psychology has 10 hits (turn indices include 168, 279 (=t280, the disclosed one), 286, 287, 288, ...); the other 3 new sessions have 0 hits. Example turn 287: text starts "um, uh, documentation. But also with psychology, because [33:46] it's such a nic..." -- a raw timestamp+speaker fragment leaked into the displayed/embedded transcript text; speakerRef itself stays correctly 'Anuradha' in all 10 cases (this is milder than the t280 defect, not a speakerRef misattribution), but it is real, undisclosed content noise flowing into this session's chunks/claims/embeddings.
reproduction: python -c "import json,re; pat=re.compile(r'\[\d{1,2}:\d{2}(?::\d{2})?\]'); turns=json.load(open('data/toc-migrated/2026-09-16-pathways-in-psychology/turns.json',encoding='utf-8')); print(sum(1 for t in turns if pat.search(t['text'])))" -> 10
fix_direction: Investigate whether this is a milder instance of the same DIARIZE_PROMPT marker-emission quirk documented in qa/contracts/diarization-marker-frequency-fix.md; if so, extend that fix's scope, or explicitly accept this as residual noise and correct the manifest's 'one-time, one-turn' framing to describe only the speakerRef-misattribution defect class, not the underlying phenomenon. Not blocking -- gap-free guard and speaker attribution both hold; this is transcript-text cosmetic noise.

title: Search reachability for 2026-09-02-india-test-series-part2 is sensitive to query phrasing: a checker-authored askV2 query similar to (but not identical with) the manifest's own query failed to retrieve it at all, citing the older, differently-scoped 2026-06-19-entrance-exams-pathways-india-part1 session instead
evidence: Checker script (scratchpad/ask-reach-check.mjs), a real askV2() call via the same production binding the manifest used (apps/api/src/production.ts's buildProductionDeps().ask). Query 'What did speakers say about India's top entrance exams like JEE and NEET?' -> verdict correct, internalSourceCount 1, citedSessionRefs ['2026-06-19-entrance-exams-pathways-india-part1'], HIT:false for the target session. A second query for the Japan session ('What did speakers say about studying in Japan, universities and language requirements?') DID correctly cite 2026-09-21-uniaccess-japan (HIT:true), matching the manifest's own claim. The manifest's own near-identically-worded India query reportedly returned internal sources:4 with a hit for the target -- not independently reproduced verbatim (2-query budget exhausted).
reproduction: Re-run a script equivalent to scratchpad/ask-reach-check.mjs with the exact query text above against tenant toc.
fix_direction: Not a data-loss or scoping defect -- the session IS correctly chunked (135), embedded and tree-indexed (confirmed via direct read-only Mongo query). This is a retrieval-quality observation: two similarly-topical India-entrance-exam sessions (2026-06-19 Part 1 and 2026-09-02 Part 2) may need better content-based disambiguation in selectNodes/ranking so a generic rephrasing doesn't always favor the older session. Track as retrieval-quality backlog, not a blocker for this ingest unit.
